description: Proof for the graph variant's Fixed layout (ECharts `series.graph.layout: 'none'`). Every panel here selects Fixed; they differ only in where the node positions come from — nowhere, the data's fixedx/fixedy columns, per-node custom.fixedX/fixedY overrides, or a mix. The first panel is the regression: Fixed used to draw an empty panel whenever the response pinned nothing, because ECharts lays a node with no `x` out at [NaN, NaN] and drops it along with every link touching it.
title: ECharts Relations — fixed layout

panels.title: Fixed layout — where the coordinates come from

options.content:
# Fixed layout

`Layout: Fixed` is ECharts' `series.graph.layout: 'none'` — the panel does no placement of its own and draws each node where its coordinates say. A node is a **field**, so those coordinates are ordinary per-mark config: `custom.fixedX` / `custom.fixedY`, reachable from the override picker like any other property, or the legacy row form's `fixedx` / `fixedy` columns.

The catch this dashboard exists for: **overrides do not exist until somebody writes them.** ECharts' `simpleLayout` does `node.setLayout([+model.get('x'), +model.get('y')])`, so a node with no `x` lays out at `[NaN, NaN]` — invisible, and so is every link that touches it. Selecting Fixed on a fresh panel therefore used to blank the visualization outright, leaving nothing on screen to drag or to write an override *against*.

So any node without a full pair is now **seeded on a ring**, in data order, exactly the way the force simulation is seeded (`force.initLayout: 'circular'`). Deterministic, so a refresh does not reshuffle the graph; already spread out, so the labels have room. Where some nodes *are* pinned, the ring goes around their bounding box, so the pinned marks keep their layout and the rest read as "not placed yet".

### The coordinate *scale* matters, which is not obvious

ECharts scales the bounding box of the emitted `x`/`y` onto the panel rect, so the shape of the point set is all that survives and any radius draws the same **nodes**. The **edges** are a different story: a graph edge is an `ECLinePath` with `subPixelOptimize: true`, and zrender shifts an axis-aligned line by half a *unit* to land a 1px stroke on a pixel centre. Those units are the graph's own space, so the seed ring used to be radius `1` and the shift was half the graph — the two edges of a four-node ring that share an x or a y were drawn 159px away from the nodes they joined. Dragging a node "fixed" it only because a drop is almost never exactly axis-aligned. The ring is pixel-ish now, so the nudge is back to being sub-pixel.

| panel | positions from |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | nothing — every node seeded |
| 2 | the data (`fixedx` / `fixedy` columns, legacy row form) |
| 3 | `custom.fixedX` / `custom.fixedY` overrides, one per node |
| 4 | two overrides; the other two nodes seeded |

Panels 1 and 4 have **Draggable nodes** on, which is what these seeds are for: drag a node to where it belongs and write that position back as an override.

panels.title: 1 · Fixed, nothing pinned — every node seeded
panels.description:
**The regression.** One edges-only query, no nodes frame, no overrides: not a single node carries `fixedX`/`fixedY`, which is the state of every panel the moment Fixed is selected. This used to render an empty canvas.

The four nodes are seeded on a ring in the order the edges name them, so the panel draws its topology and the user has something to drag. Refresh the dashboard — the layout does not move, because the seed is data order rather than `Math.random()`.

panels.title: 2 · Fixed, pinned by the data
panels.description:
The route the node-graph row form has always had: a nodes frame with `fixedx` / `fixedy` columns, converted to the wide contract above the panel (`converters/legacyToWide.ts`). Every node pins both, which is also what makes Fixed the layout the panel would have inferred on its own with `Layout` left unset.

The coordinate space is arbitrary for the **nodes** — ECharts takes the bounding box of the emitted `x`/`y` and scales it onto the panel rect (`createViewCoordSys`), so what survives is the *shape* of the point set. Its **scale** still matters for the edges: pick a range like 0–1 and zrender's sub-pixel optimization shifts every axis-aligned edge half a unit off its nodes. See the note above.

panels.title: 3 · Fixed, pinned by per-node overrides
panels.description:
The same four positions as panel 2, written as **field overrides** rather than carried in the response — `custom.fixedX` / `custom.fixedY` under a `byName` matcher, one pair per node. This is only addressable because a node is a field: the row form could not express it without changing the query.

It is also the shape a "remember where I dragged this node" feature writes, which is why it gets a panel of its own.

**Needs `grafana.panelPluginTransformations`** on an edges-only response like this one — the nodes are declared as fields above the panel by `converters/deriveNodes.ts`, and without that pass there is no field for a `byName` override to land on, so this panel falls back to panel 1's seeded ring.

panels.title: 4 · Fixed, half pinned — the two halves coexist
panels.description:
`gateway` and `db` carry `custom.fixedX` / `custom.fixedY`; `api` and `web` carry nothing. This is the state a panel is in halfway through positioning a topology by hand, and it has to draw — the old all-or-nothing reading dropped the unpinned two and both links between them.

The seeded pair goes on a ring **around** the pinned bounding box rather than inside it, so which nodes are placed and which are not is readable at a glance. Drag one and it joins the pinned set.

panels.title: 5 · Drag a node — the position is written back as an override
panels.description:
**Drag one of these nodes.** The panel writes the layout **as drawn** into `custom.fixedX` / `custom.fixedY` overrides — every node, not just the one that moved — exactly as the legend's colour picker writes a fixed colour. Every node, because the unpinned ones are seeded around whichever nodes *are* pinned: recording the first drag alone re-seeded all its neighbours around it, so moving one node rearranged the whole topology. Open the Overrides tab afterwards and they are all there, editable and clearable like any other override; the dashboard shows unsaved changes until you save it.

Both frames are already **wide** (one field per node, one field per edge), so unlike panels 3 and 4 this needs no pre-pass and works on any host. A node with no field is fine too: the panel reads its position back out of the override by name, so an edges-only response remembers a drag as well.

**Remember view** is on here too. Pan the graph (drag the background) or use the corner zoom buttons and the view is written into the panel's options rather than forgotten on reload.
